chapter_theme: Path Saivism (மார்க்க சைவம்): the means and the vision of the pure Saiva, who holds Vedanta and Siddhanta as one, reflects on the Lord, the soul, the bond and release, and by the feet of the Supreme power becomes Siva, while soul and bond cannot of themselves reach the Lord.
structure_note: Means and marks of the pure Saiva (1427 to 1429); the Supreme power and the state beyond real and unreal (1430, 1431); what the pure Saiva contemplates and sees (1432 to 1434); the schools compared (1435); the limit of soul and bond (1436); and the attainment of Siddhanta (1437). Despite the heading, most verses speak of the pure Saiva.

1427.reading: For pure Saivas the means are Siva's emblem of gold, the sacred ash, the good path, great knowledge, the means by which the wrong path does not arise, and the true path.
1427.nuance: சாதனம் is both a means of practice and an emblem worn, and the verse may mean either or both. பூதி is sacred ash. சன்மார்க்கம், the true path, is in Siddhanta the path of knowledge. பொன்னாற் சிவசாதனம் may be a gold emblem or Siva's emblem made precious.

1428.reading: The faultless knower, lord of rising knowledge, in whom knowledge dawns within the joined portion of Vedanta and Siddhanta, who has true release, is the eternal devotee of pure Saivism.
1428.nuance: வேதாந்த சித்தாந்த, written as one compound, treats the two as a single body of teaching. சத்தசைவம் is read as சுத்த சைவம்; சத்த could also be 'true'.

1429.reading: The Agamas are nine, and within them the twenty-eight, free of delusion, in their three divisions; pure Saivism is the rare whole in which they and the calm truth of Vedanta and Siddhanta end as one.
1429.nuance: Twenty-eight (நாலேழு, four sevens) is the standard count of Saiva Agamas; the nine are those Tirumular names in his preface (63). The two நாலேழு and the three divisions (முப்பேதம்) are not clear, and the counting may be compressed.

1430.reading: The Supreme power who stands apart from the pure and the impure, the seven turiya states, the real and the unreal, she who impels and she who is within, is the Father's power of grace and is everywhere.
1430.nuance: பராபரை is the feminine of பராபரன், the Supreme as Shakti; it is repeated three times with different qualifiers. துரியங்கள் ஓரேழு, seven turiyas, can't be fixed from the verse. அருட்சத்தி names grace as the Lord's own power.

1431.reading: Those who have passed beyond the real and the unreal become that very one, in the state of 'I am Siva' where sentient and insentient are no longer told apart, and sink into the power of bliss in release; attainment too is at its height there.
1431.nuance: சிவோகம் (I am Siva) is a contemplative formula; Siddhanta tradition takes it as union in which the soul does not cease, a reading the verse alone does not settle. தானாகி may mean they become themselves or become Him.

1432.reading: What pure Saivas are to reflect on is the self, the Supreme called Sadasiva, the abiding triad of Lord, soul and bond, the ancient stainless-making impurity and the bondage from before, and release.
1432.nuance: The list is the syllabus of Siddhanta: self, Lord, the three categories, impurity, bondage and release. மாசற்ற may qualify what follows (the soul made stainless) or the whole list; பழமலம், the ancient impurity, is traditionally anava, beginningless as 115 says.

1433.reading: For pure Saivas the vision is this: when all is set in the fullness and cut away, death comes to its end, and with bliss there is the long enjoyment of the twelve.
1433.nuance: மாரணம் may be 'death' or 'great death'; ஈராறு (twelve) and நீதி are unexplained, and the second and third lines are obscure. Only the frame, a vision of fullness and bliss, is fairly sure.

1434.reading: To hold to unchanging knowledge and great yoga without pride, settle the unsettled mind and make it Siva, and keep to the path by cherishing the contemplation one has gained: that, marked out, is the jnani's charya.
1434.nuance: சரிதை is சரியை, service, here named as the service proper to the jnani: tradition nests each of the four paths within the others. மதிப்பற may be 'without pride' or 'beyond measure'. பாவனை, contemplation, is what the jnani keeps up as his service.

1435.reading: Those who have seen Vedanta hold that Brahman alone is real and the world false; those who have seen the end of nada are yogis who do not waver; and the Siddhanta that is not other than Vedanta is the way Saivas share.
1435.nuance: பிரமமித்தியாதரர் is read as those who hold Brahman (பிரமம்) and falsity (மித்யா), the Advaita thesis that the world is false; that division is the tradition's. வேதாந்தம் அல்லாத சித்தாந்தம் can mean a Siddhanta not other than Vedanta or one that is not Vedanta, and the two readings pull opposite ways. சாதாரணமன்ன is likewise 'common' or 'like the common'.

1436.reading: As clouds do not reach the sky and the many sights do not reach the eye, the Lord, who is thought of yet beyond the reach of thought, is not reached by soul and bond.
1436.nuance: The images make the relation one-way: the sky holds the clouds, the eye takes in the sights, and neither is reached by what it holds. The last line repeats 115's பதியினைச் சென்றணுகா பசு பாசம் with அண்ணல் for பதி.

1437.reading: To be neither one nor two nor nothing, yet one; to leave the sects and the formless; and to go by her feet to the love of the Supreme power and so become Siva: that is the attainment of Siddhanta.
1437.nuance: ஒன்றும் இரண்டும் இலதுமாய் is the Siddhanta formula of non-duality, neither simple oneness nor two, as tradition reads it. நிராகாரம் may be the formless as a doctrine held by some sect. பாதத்தால் may be by her feet or on foot.

links.note: 115 states that pasu and pasam cannot reach the Lord; 1436 repeats the line and gives it images, clouds that never reach the sky and sights that never reach the eye. It leaves out 115's other half, that when the Lord approaches they cease.
115 sets out Pati, Pasu and Pasam as beginningless; 1432 makes that triad, with impurity and release, the matter the pure Saiva contemplates.
63 names the nine Agamas Nandi received (Karanam, Kamikam and the rest); 1429 begins from the same nine before naming the twenty-eight.
1420's pure Saiva discerns the real, the unreal and what is both, and keeps clear of the sentient and the insentient; 1431's has passed beyond them, into a state where they are no longer told apart.
Both make the feet the way: in the Kural reaching the Lord's feet takes one across the sea of births; in Tirumular going by the feet of the Supreme power one becomes Siva.

source_issues: 1431: line 1 reads அசுத்து where 1420 and 1430 have அசத்து; probably a misprint, though அசுத்தம் (impure) would also make sense.
1433: lines 2 and 3 (மாரண மந்த மதித்தானந் தத்தோடு / நேரென ஈராறு நீதி நெடும் போகங்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
Chapter 89 is headed மார்க்க சைவம் but most of its verses describe the pure Saiva (சுத்த சைவர்).
